target.title: fix(cron): preserve script state and stop stale runs after restart
target.body:
Closes #111271
Closes #111272
Closes #111273
Closes #111274

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes several cron script regressions where successful state updates could be lost on manual, startup catch-up, or crash-recovery runs; main-target script work could survive cancellation/restart boundaries and emit stale notify or wake effects; and model-authored flat script arguments could be dropped or misclassified as agent turns.

It also makes the live cron restart scenario fail closed instead of retrying stateful job creation in the same gateway, and records enough evidence to distinguish one-off, recurring, restart, and delivery behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron script payloads now share one detached-execution classification and one successful-state application path across scheduled, manual, startup, and task-ledger recovery flows. The task ledger carries internal script state through crash recovery, while late script results recheck both cancellation and scheduler-generation ownership before notify/wake side effects.

Flat cron recovery now recognizes `script` and `toolBudget` and gives script content precedence over generic agent-turn timeout hints. The stateful live QA scenario disables whole-scenario retries, allows overhead beyond cron's intentional two-minute startup deferral, rejects extra jobs, and reports reconstructible schedule/run/restart/delivery facts.

## User Impact

Operators can cancel main-target script jobs reliably, restart the gateway without old script results notifying afterward, and expect successful script state to survive every execution and recovery path. Models using flat cron arguments can create and update script jobs without losing script-specific fields.

## Evidence

- Live OpenAI GPT-5.4 run on isolated gateway port `54542`: exactly two native cron tool calls; one randomized `at` job and one randomized 20-second `every` job.
- One-off: `one-shot-runs=1`, removed after success.
- Recurring: 11 successful runs, still enabled, next run advanced from `1784446205400` to `1784446570069`.
- Restart: same address before/after (`http://127.0.0.1:54542`), with a later successful recurring run.
- Final state: exactly one job; zero outbound messages containing either randomized cron payload marker.
- Source-blind artifact validation: all eight contract clauses passed.
- Focused tests: 198 passed across cron runtime, flat tool arguments, and QA catalog.
- Stress: 20/20 repeated runs of the six new regression cases passed.
- Static gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview after the final rebase: no findings; patch correct at 0.88 confidence.
- A fresh remote Testbox could not start because its GitHub Actions shell-preparation step failed before checkout; trusted-source validation therefore used the documented local fallback.
